questions.question: My co-founder sued me in federal court over our founders' stock purchase agreement, which has a written clause sending disputes under it to arbitration. I would rather arbitrate. What can I ask the federal court to do, and is there a notice requirement?

In an arbitration under the Federal Arbitration Act between our startup and a seed investor, we need the company's former outside accountant, who is not a party, to appear at the hearing and bring the accounting workpapers. Can the arbitrator require that, and if the accountant ignores it, which court can compel attendance?

An arbitrator just delivered an award against me in a dispute with my co-founder, and our agreement is governed by the Federal Arbitration Act. I think the arbitrator was biased. How long do I have to serve notice of a motion to vacate the award?

A seed investor filed a federal securities fraud suit under the Exchange Act against our startup and both founders over statements in our pitch deck, and we have moved to dismiss. Can the investor take discovery while the motion is pending, and in the meantime what are we required to do with our documents and data?

Our startup just received a letter saying a federal agency has opened an inquiry into how we raised our seed round. My co-founder suggests wiping an old company laptop that holds investor emails before anyone asks for it. What federal criminal statute would that risk, and what is the maximum prison term?
mustNot: (up to|not more than|maximum of|maximum term of) (5|five|10|ten) years

questions.question: A co-founder and I are arbitrating under the Colorado Uniform Arbitration Act. Can the arbitrator subpoena our former bookkeeper, who is not a party, to bring the company's records to the hearing, and can the arbitrator allow depositions? If the bookkeeper refuses, who enforces the subpoena?

We lost an arbitration under the Colorado Uniform Arbitration Act against a seed investor and received notice of the award last week. What is the deadline to ask a Colorado court to vacate it, and does the clock change if we later learn the award was procured by fraud?

The arbitration clause in our investor rights agreement expressly says the Delaware Uniform Arbitration Act applies. A copy of the award against us was delivered yesterday. How long do we have to apply to the Court of Chancery to vacate it, and is there a different clock if the award was procured by fraud?

For a side letter between our Delaware startup and a venture fund investor, we want disputes to go to arbitration under the Delaware Rapid Arbitration Act. What does the clause have to include for that Act to apply, and what rights do the parties give up by agreeing to it?

A co-founder served as a director and the chief executive officer of our Delaware corporation and has since moved out of state and left both roles. If the company sues him in Delaware for breaching his fiduciary duties, can he still be served there, and how?
